content.user_title: Add Tool Lifecycle UI to AI Apps
content.value_statement: AI apps need clear status for tool calls, approvals, results, and errors. This skill provides React and Next.js component guidance for visible tool lifecycles.
actual_capabilities: Shows ToolCall usage for pending and running tool states.
Shows ToolResult usage for completed tool outputs.
Shows ToolApproval usage for human approval and denial flows.
Documents automatic icon choices based on tool name patterns.
Includes an Agent component example that renders tool lifecycle states.
limitations: Does not implement backend tool execution or permission checks.
Requires React or Next.js and compatible UI component setup.
Uses external install commands that should be reviewed before running.
Does not provide tests, source components, or package lock files in this skill.

use_cases.title: Add Tool Status Cards
use_cases.description: Add visible pending, running, success, error, and approval states to an AI chat interface.

use_cases.title: Review Approval Workflows
use_cases.description: Design clear approval screens before tools send messages, edit files, or call external services.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Tool Displays
use_cases.description: Create consistent visual patterns for tool arguments, results, icons, and failures across an agent product.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Tool Status UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tools-ui skill to add a ToolCall display for pending, running, success, error, and approval states in my React app.

prompt_templates.title: Create Approval Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tools-ui skill to design a ToolApproval flow for tools that send email, edit files, or call external APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Tool Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tools-ui skill to show ToolResult cards for search, file read, and API results in a Next.js agent interface.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Full Agent Tool Surface
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tools-ui skill to map my agent tools to status, approval, result, icon, and error UI states.

output_examples.input: Request: Add a visible state display for an agent search tool.
output_examples.output: A plan for a tool call card with running, success, and error states, plus placement guidance.

output_examples.input: Request: Add approval before tools send messages.
output_examples.output: A human approval layout with approve and deny actions, argument review, and result display after execution.

output_examples.input: Request: Standardize icons for common tool names.
output: Search tools use a search icon.
File read tools use a file icon.
Message tools use a mail icon.

best_practices: Require human approval for tools that send messages, modify files, or call paid services.
Show the tool name, arguments, status, and final result in one consistent area.
Review remote installation output before committing generated component files.
anti_patterns: Hide tool execution details from users when actions affect external systems.
Run install commands from the skill without checking the remote registry first.
Use success styling before the tool result is received and validated.

faq.question: Does this skill execute tools for me?
faq.answer: No. It documents UI components for displaying tool lifecycle states. Your app still controls execution and permissions.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content targets compatible AI coding assistants and React or Next.js projects.

faq.question: Does it include approval controls?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a ToolApproval pattern with approve and deny handlers.

faq.question: Does it provide backend APIs?
faq.answer: No. You must provide tool execution, authorization, and audit logging in your application.

faq.question: Are remote install commands required?
faq.answer: The documentation uses remote install examples. Review the registry content before running them in a project.

faq.question: What UI states are covered?
faq.answer: It covers pending, running, approval, success, and error states for tool calls.
